drafted_from: tool:trade-an-x-sign-in-code-for-its-tokens's row in tools/connect-a-service-and-seal-its-key/tool-rows.json (job, description, input_schema, invoke) and the folder's test/connect-by-signing-in.test.mjs, whose stand-in answers give the reply and the held word
start_here: Say to your AI: "Trade an X sign-in code for its tokens for the new connection service_connection:x:sams_bakery with the code made-up-code-4f9a2c." It runs tool:trade-an-x-sign-in-code-for-its-tokens and tells you the tokens are kept in the vault without showing any of them.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it sends one request to X for the connection it is handed and keeps the tokens in the vault as that connection's fields.
instructions: 1. Do not run this by hand: tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service runs it for you at the sign-in callback, after you open the sign-in address it gave you. Start that tool first (its kit shows the call) and keep the connection_id it answers: service_connection:x:sams_bakery is the shape.

2. To run this step alone, the AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:trade-an-x-sign-in-code-for-its-tokens and the input the worked example shows (the connection by its handle only, the code the service handed back, the callback address the sign-in was started with and the PKCE verifier).

3. Read what comes back: the service's reply with every kept token already replaced by the word [held]. The access and refresh tokens now sit in the vault as the connection's own fields; neither is in the answer.
4. A refusal (a used-up code, a wrong callback address) is shown as the service's own error; nothing is kept, so start the sign-in again for a new link.

worked_examples.title: Trade an X sign-in code for its tokens for a made-up connection
worked_examples.ask: Trade an X sign-in code for its tokens for service_connection:x:sams_bakery.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/connect-a-service-and-seal-its-key/tool-rows.json and the x descriptor in records.json (Basic client authentication, PKCE, the scopes asked, an access token that lasts two hours, offline.access returns a refresh token); the held word "[held]" is the one test/connect-by-signing-in.test.mjs uses; the folder test has no stand-in for X's reply, so this is the reply the descriptor's notes describe. Input: {"connection":{"connection_id":"service_connection:x:sams_bakery"},"code":"made-up-code-4f9a2c","redirect_uri":"https://app.gettrillion.ai/work/api/connect/callback","code_verifier":"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ABCDEFG"}.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"token_type":"bearer","expires_in":7200,"access_token":"[held]","scope":"tweet.read tweet.write users.read bookmark.read like.read offline.access","refresh_token":"[held]"}. The access and refresh tokens now sit in the vault as the connection's own fields; neither is in the answer.
